name: Processing Fluency as Monitoring Node
citation: Reber, R., Schwarz, N., & Winkielman, P. (2004). Processing fluency and aesthetic pleasure. Personality and Social Psychology Review, 8(4), 364-382.

constructs.description: Metacognitive monitoring signal reflecting ease of processing. Integrates prediction error magnitude, perceptual organization cost, and metabolic efficiency.
Processing fluency generates positive affect via misattribution — ease of processing is interpreted as familiarity, safety, or aesthetic quality.
Fluency influences truth judgments, preference judgments, and aesthetic evaluations through a common metacognitive pathway.

schema_gaps: Individual differences in fluency sensitivity unmodeled
Cultural variation in fluency-affect link strength unmodeled
Disfluency-as-signal effects (novelty, difficulty = engagement) not captured
irreducible_residual.narrative: Processing fluency reduces well to PP prediction error monitoring + IC metabolic cost tracking + NM reward signals. However, the metacognitive attribution step (interpreting fluency AS preference/truth/beauty) involves IE-DPT implicit-explicit boundary crossing that is not fully mechanized. The disfluency literature (Alter & Oppenheimer, 2009) shows fluency is not always positive — strategic disfluency can enhance learning and engagement.
